parsed.explanation: Local protections are strong and documented, but the combined regime is gated nationally: entry screening can refuse on document/presentation discrepancy and raise permanent fraud ineligibility, passports have been confiscated/blocked, and federal facilities bar identity-congruent access. State bathroom, anti-discrimination, hate-crime and shield-care laws mitigate life after admission, yet do not govern entry, federal facilities or federal custody, where documented conversion-therapy, hormone denial and immigration-custody abuse occur. Litigation creates uncertainty but Supreme Court allowance of passport restrictions is operative.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport rule, X-marker processing stopped, Supreme Court allowed restrictions; entry cable directs refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; passport suit pending. No state protection governs national documents.
entry_documents.interaction: State marker/self-attestation and local ID do not alter foreign ministry screening; entry decision is first, dispositive encounter and can strand visitor before state protections apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopted conversion-therapy model: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for federal/immigration detention. State hate-crime and anti-discrimination laws do not govern national custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger investigation/detention, then birth-sex placement/care denial in national custody; state remedies do not reach that system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State itself has no mapped ban and single-occupancy restrooms are gender-neutral; largest city ordinance allows self-determined bathroom access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law since 2006, gender-neutral single-occupancy law 2020, city all-gender school bathrooms since 2021; May 2023 multi-occupancy bill status unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State/local access operates for state/private venues, but federal buildings/airports remain under national ban; traveller must navigate both regimes.

care_services.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care, funding, and record subpoenas; hospital-ward/federal facility placement by birth sex may out traveller. Adult routine care locally not documented as barred.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law expressly protects care lawful in state for travellers from out-of-state, patients and providers; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2016.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects state care provision but not federal facilities, national insurance/funding rules, or outside-state subpoena risk, which dossier says is unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive framing as binary at birth, 'gender ideology' removal, counterterrorism priority discussion of 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 66% poll support for birth-sex documents. One documented bathroom trespass arrest nationally, not in this state.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime enhancement since 2015, panic defence repealed 2018, most-protective tier ranking; national hate-crime statute exists but only 23 states cover gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing and enforcement priorities raise entry/federal encounter risk despite state protective laws and court challenges enjoining some orders.

minors_guardians.exposure: National sports entry ban, orders to investigate/prosecute facilitation of minor social transition, youth-care bans in 27 states, hospital subpoenas nationally. Accompanying minor could face school/facility and care exposure at federal/national level.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law covers care for travelling patients, conversion-therapy ban for minors, school bullying/privacy protections and 2019 task force on names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.interaction: State shield mitigates state care/school life, but does not cancel federal funding, investigation, sports-entry or custody rules affecting a travelling family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Airport screening can be invasive and outing; national public opinion is divided/hostile on birth-sex documents. No state-specific trans violence, police abuse or prosecution data documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State discrimination banned in public accommodations since 2006, hate-crime penalties, jury-selection ban; ranking is legislative, not outcome evidence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse may operate for street/public-accommodation incidents, but police at border/federal custody are national actors with documented hostile practices.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order litigation unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined but current operative status varies by measure; appeal of entry refusal slow and rarely successful is not documented for this exact cable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit on passports, legal-aid FAQ, state courts/anti-discrimination and hate-crime mechanisms; shield-law resilience to outside subpoenas not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist in parallel systems: state remedies do not compel federal entry, federal facilities or national custody, so traveller remedy depends on which sovereign controls the encounter.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine, discretionary entry exclusion for visibly trans travellers with weak appeal prospects, but lower than 0.35 because refusal is not documented as universal for all trans visitors, fraud ineligibility is not automatic, and state life after admission is strongly protective.

Similar border secondary screening and administrative refusal risk, but lower than 0.55 because national passport restrictions are Supreme-Court-allowed, confiscations/stranding are documented, federal facilities are barred, and national custody abuse is documented.

Lower than 0.65: in that anchor national equality law protected the visitor and produced apology/compensation after brief holding. Here national law itself restricts markers/facilities, courts allowed passport restriction, and no equivalent federal remedy is documented.

parsed.synthesis: After admission, the state regime is protective: identity-congruent local facilities, discrimination/hate-crime laws and shield care materially raise safety. The combined journey, however, begins with national screening that can refuse entry or trigger permanent fraud consequences, continues through federal facilities barred by birth sex, and ends in national custody with documented severe abuse if detained. State protections do not pre-empt those federal exposures, so the operative risk is elevated, below the 0.55 border-friction anchor but above routine state-level exclusion.
